text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Bilious vomiting. I also have Feeding intolerance, No fever, Vomiting started within first day after birth.

speaker: Patient
text: Physical examination shows epicanthus, upward slanting of the eyelids, low-set ears, and a single transverse palmar crease. A grade 2/6 holosystolic murmur heard at the left mid to lower sternal border. The lungs are clear to auscultation. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Based on the physical findings of epicanthus, upward-slanting palpebral fissures, low-set ears, a single transverse palmar crease, and a holosystolic murmur, please confirm if there is a history of polyhydramnios or any known maternal diabetes. While these features strongly suggest a genetic syndrome like Down syndrome, the bilious vomiting and feeding intolerance require immediate surgical evaluation for midgut volvulus or malrotation; I have already requested an Abdominal X-Ray.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Down Syndrome (Trisomy 21) with suspected Malrotation with Midgut Volvulus
